Attachment.description: A picture as a message refers to it: the stored hash, and the name it was given.
Attachment.title: Attachment

ColoursIn.description:
Dress a weft in a pair of colours, or send nulls to give it back to the theme.
One without the other is refused — a gradient with one end is not a gradient.
ColoursIn.title: ColoursIn

EngineIn.description:
Bind a weft to a provider and a model, or unbind it.

Both or neither, like the voice: a provider with no model has nothing to ask for,
and a model with no provider has nowhere to be asked.
EngineIn.title: EngineIn

HeaderRow.description:
One extra request header. Checked properly by ``upstream.clean_headers``; the
lengths here only stop a body from being enormous before that runs.
HeaderRow.title: HeaderRow

HeadersIn.description:
Replace the extra headers a weft sends upstream. An empty list removes them.

The whole list every time, like the history dials: the page holds the set, and a
patch-one-row endpoint would need an identity for a row that has none but its name.
HeadersIn.title: HeadersIn

HistoryIn.description:
Set how a weft's conversation is kept, how much is sent, and how much is held.

Every field is required rather than optional-with-a-default. This endpoint replaces
the set, and a partial update would let a client that only knew about some of them
silently reset the rest to defaults the user never chose.

``send_turns`` is allowed to exceed ``window_turns`` and is deliberately NOT clamped
to it. The effective cap is the smaller of the two, but the number the user typed is
the number that gets stored, so raising the window later finds their choice still
waiting rather than quietly rewritten behind their back.
HistoryIn.title: HistoryIn

MarkOut.description: One tip this account has finished: a done tip, or a found hidden one.
MarkOut.title: MarkOut

PickHistory.description:
Whether a pick keeps a copy of its conversation on the device showing it.

`memory` is the default and means what Weft has always done: a reload empties the
window. `local` means the browser keeps a scrollback so a refresh does not wipe what
you were reading.

`session` (2026-10-04) means the conversation lives in a session store: a
memory-mcp-ce server the user added as a `session` provider. The service relays the
thread to and from it and keeps nothing itself. The service still stores no conversation, because
relaying is not storing: the store is upstream, like the gateway, and every device
that opens the pick sees the same thread because the store has it.

None of these values stores anything HERE. The service keeps no
conversation, and `local` is a copy in one browser that never reaches this side of
the glass. What is stored in this column is the *choice*, which is furniture — the
same argument the voice columns below already make.
PickHistory.title: PickHistory

ProviderIn.description:
The Add form. ``secret`` is optional because a gateway on the private network
often needs no bearer at all, and requiring one would mean inventing a placeholder
that then gets sent upstream.
ProviderIn.title: ProviderIn

ProviderKind.description:
What a stored endpoint is for.

`llm` is an OpenAI-compatible chat/models endpoint. `tts` is a speech endpoint
— the same `/v1`-shaped surface, but answering `/audio/speech` instead
of `/chat/completions`. Both live in this one table because they are the same thing
from the vault's point of view: somebody else's URL and somebody else's key.

`session` is a memory-mcp-ce server whose `/v1/sessions` API stores conversations
(2026-10-04). Same table for the same reason: a URL and a key that are somebody
else's, sealed in the vault, opened only by the service.

An enum rather than a free string so the picker can filter on it without a
magic-value convention, and so adding `stt` later is a migration rather than a
convention nobody wrote down.
ProviderKind.title: ProviderKind

ProviderPatch.description:
The Edit form. Every field optional, and ``secret`` has three meanings:

* absent / ``null`` — leave the stored token alone. This is what the form sends
  when the user did not type in the blank token field, and it is why an edit does
  not require re-entering a secret nobody can read back.
* ``""`` — clear it. The provider then sends no Authorization header.
* anything else — replace it.
ProviderPatch.title: ProviderPatch

Role.description:
Three levels, and the gap between them is the whole authorization model.

owner  — exactly one at bootstrap; the only role that may grant `admin` or change
         anyone's role. The single privilege-escalation path in the service.
admin  — may create and deactivate users and mint `user` invites. May NOT change
         roles, and may not read anyone's vault.
user   — owns their own providers and nothing else.
Role.title: Role

SessionOut.description: One signed-in device, as the Account screen shows it.
SessionOut.title: SessionOut

SttIn.description: The whole settings block, replaced at once, as the Settings form sends it.
SttIn.title: SttIn

VoiceIn.description: Give a weft a voice, or take it away. All three or none.
VoiceIn.title: VoiceIn

WeftIn.description: Add a weft. The name is all it needs; the engine can be given now or later.
WeftIn.title: WeftIn

WeftOut.description:
One weft, everything about it. The Pick menu and the weft page read the same
shape, so a value set on one is never missing from the other.
WeftOut.title: WeftOut

WeftPatch.description: Rename a weft. The only thing about it that is not its own section.
WeftPatch.title: WeftPatch

put.description:
Store one picture for a message that is about to be sent.

The body is the picture itself, as for a background: a raw body is what lets the
size cap bite while it streams. SVG is refused (markup that can carry script), and
what is stored is never what was sent; see app/backgrounds.py.

get.description:
One of the caller's own pictures.

Looked up under the caller's own directory, so a hash someone else uploaded gets the
same 404 as one nobody did. Cacheable forever, privately: the name is the hash of
the bytes.

Issue a CSRF token as both a readable cookie and a body value.

Called by the client before its first state-changing request. Unauthenticated by
necessity: login is itself a protected POST, so a token has to be obtainable before
anyone is logged in. That is safe because the token proves nothing about identity —
it only proves the request was made by script running on our own origin.

schema.title: Response Get Csrf Api Auth Csrf Get

post.description:
Authenticate and start a session.

Every failure below returns the same 401 with the same body, and takes comparable
time. The rate-limit rejection is the one exception — it returns 429 with
Retry-After, because telling a locked-out user to come back later is useful to them
and tells an attacker only what they already know.

End this device's session.

Authenticates from the refresh cookie, NOT from an access token, so it still works
after the access token has expired — which is the common case, because people log
out after leaving a tab open overnight.

Always returns 200, even for an unknown or absent cookie. Logging out is not a
thing that should be able to fail, and reporting "no such session" would confirm
which tokens are real.

schema.title: Response Logout Api Auth Logout Post

post.description:
End every session for this account, on every device.

Two steps, and BOTH are required:

1. Revoke every refresh family — stops new access tokens being minted.
2. Bump ``token_version`` — invalidates every access token already out there.

Doing only the first leaves a window of up to the access-token TTL in which a
stolen token still works, which defeats the point of the button. ``tv`` exists
precisely to close that window.

schema.title: Response Logout All Api Auth Logout All Post

get.description:
Who am I.

Uses the unrestricted dependency so a bootstrap credential can render the
"you must change your password" screen instead of getting a 409 it cannot explain.

post.description:
Change your own password.

Requires the current password even though the caller is already authenticated:
that is what stops a stolen access token, or an XSS holding one, from locking the
real owner out of their own account.

On success every *other* session is ended. The device doing the change keeps
working — logging someone out for successfully securing their account trains them
not to.

schema.title: Response Change Password Api Auth Password Post

post.description:
Rotate the refresh token and mint a fresh access token.

On ANY failure the refresh cookie is cleared. Leaving a rejected cookie in place
would have the client retry it forever — and if the rejection was reuse detection,
every retry looks like another attack.

get.description: Every device this account is signed in on, this one first.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api Auth Sessions Get

delete.description:
Sign one device out. Its next request is refused, not merely its next refresh.

404 for a device that is not yours, already signed out, or never existed — one
answer for all three, so an id cannot be probed for. Ending the device you are on is
allowed and is the same as /logout, cookies and all.

schema.title: Response End Session Api Auth Sessions  Session Id  Delete

post.description: Relay one turn of conversation to whatever the weft is bound to.

get.description:
The page an invite points at: mints the weft's key and serves the guide, once.

Read by the agent, which has no Weft login: the address is the credential. Markdown,
because a model reads it. A second read gets a 410, which says the invite existed
and is gone, rather than a 404 that could be a typo.

delete.description: Close every one of this user's doors at once.

put.description:
Store a picture sent to a one-time address from the ``upload`` tool.

The address is used up by trying it, whether the picture turns out to be one or
not: a second try needs a second address. The content type is not consulted.
``curl -T`` sends none, and every byte is decoded and re-encoded anyway, which is
what refuses a file that is not a picture (app/backgrounds.py).

get.description: One weft's waiting notifications, newest first.

parameters.description: The weft whose notifications to list.
parameters.name: weft

schema.description: The weft whose notifications to list.
schema.title: Weft
Response List Notifications Api Notifications Get

get.description: How many notifications each weft has waiting. Wefts with none are left out.

post.description: Dismiss every notification one weft has waiting.

schema.title: Response Dismiss All Api Notifications Dismiss Post

delete.description: Dismiss one notification. It is gone, on every device.

get.description:
Every provider this user owns, oldest first, each with how many wefts it answers.

``selectinload`` on the wefts turns what would be one query per row into two
queries total. With a handful of providers that is not a performance concern; it is
here so the N+1 never gets written in the first place.

schema.title: Response List Providers Api Providers Get

post.description:
Add a provider.

The row id is generated here rather than left to the column default because the
vault's associated data binds the ciphertext to it — the id has to exist before the
secret can be sealed. See ``app/vault.py`` for why that binding is worth the
awkwardness.

delete.description:
Remove a provider. The wefts it answered stay, unbound.

The database's ON DELETE SET NULL does the unbinding. A weft with no engine is
still on the Pick menu with everything it owns, waiting for a new one.

patch.description: Edit a provider. Omitting ``secret`` leaves the stored token untouched.

get.description:
Fetch this provider's live model list, and say which wefts use which.

This is the only route in the service that opens a sealed secret, and the only one
that makes an outbound request. Both facts are worth keeping true: if a second
route needs either, that is the moment to ask whether it should go through here.

What a speech provider can say, and in whose voice.

Two upstream calls, because the OpenAI speech protocol splits them: ``/models`` names
the engine and ``/audio/voices`` names the voice, and ``/audio/speech`` wants both.

Where one weft's session ends, and nothing else.

The cheap question a window asks every few seconds while it is open: "has another
device added to this thread?" It reads one row's summary in the store — no event,
nothing decrypted — so polling it costs next to nothing at either end. When the
answer differs from what the window last read, the window asks /thread.

The tail of one weft's session, as many turns as its window holds.

With ``after_seq``, a catch-up instead: only the messages after that seq, for a
window that already holds the thread up to it. This is the read the window makes
when /head says the session has moved on, and it is cheap where the tail is not:
the store decrypts every event it returns, so a long thread's tail costs tens of
seconds and the two events a new exchange added cost milliseconds.

A catch-up falls back to the tail (``full: true``) when it cannot be one: the
session ends before ``after_seq`` (it was replaced or cleared), or more happened
since than a catch-up reads.

post.description: Say one reply in the voice its thread was given.

get.description:
The user's push-to-talk settings. The window asks on mount, to know whether to
show the 🎤 petal at all.

What a speech-to-text provider says it can run. Empty when it will not say: the
user can still type a model name, and many servers ignore it anyway.

post.description:
Turn one recording into words, with the user's own provider.

The body is the recording itself, with the content type the browser recorded it in
(``audio/webm`` from Chrome, ``audio/mp4`` from Safari).

get.description: Every tip, in file order, and this account's progress through them.

post.description: Mark tips finished. Unknown ids are ignored, and so is one already done.

schema.title: Response Finish Tips Api Tips Done Post

put.description: Tips on or off, for this account on every device.

schema.title: Response Switch Tips Api Tips On Put

post.description: Start again. Restarting the help turns tips back on; forgetting finds does not.

get.description:
Every weft this user has, by name. This is the Pick menu.

Reads no secrets and makes no outbound call, so opening the chat costs one indexed
query, not a round trip to every gateway the user has configured.

schema.title: Response List Wefts Api Wefts Get

post.description: Add a weft by name. It is on the Pick menu from this moment, engine or not.

get.description:
A background picture — only to someone with a weft wearing it.

A picture that exists but is not the caller's gets the same 404 as one that does not
exist, so the route cannot be used to ask whether somebody else has uploaded a given
image. Cacheable forever, privately: the name is the hash of the bytes.

delete.description:
Delete a weft and everything it owns. The only route that can.

Its picture goes too once nothing else wears it. A thread kept in a session store
is not touched: that store is upstream, and its contents are not ours to delete.

patch.description: Rename a weft. Its thread stays put: the session id does not follow the name.

delete.description: Take this weft's picture away. The file goes too, once nothing else wears it.

put.description:
Give this weft a background picture, replacing any it had.

The body is the picture itself, not a form, so the size cap bites while it streams.
The content type must say it is an image — and SVG, which is one, is refused,
because it is markup that can carry script. What is stored is never what was sent;
see app/backgrounds.py.

Set the pair of colours this weft wears, or clear it back to the theme's.
Stored lowercase, so "#ABCDEF" and "#abcdef" are the same colour twice.

delete.description: Close this weft's door: its key stops working, and so do its upload addresses.

get.description: Whether this weft's door is open, and since when.

post.description: Mint this weft's key, replacing any it had. The old key stops working at once.

A one-time address to hand the weft's agent in the chat.

Reading it mints the key and serves the guide, so the key itself never passes
through the chat. Any invite this weft already had waiting stops working.

put.description:
Say which provider and model answer this weft, or that nothing does.

Everything else about the weft stays as it was. That is the point of the shape: the
same weft on a new engine keeps its colours, voice, picture and thread.

Set the extra HTTP headers this weft sends with its chat requests.

Not secrets, and treated as not secrets: they are shown back in the clear. The
names that carry a credential, or describe the request itself, are refused (see
``upstream.RESERVED_HEADERS``), so a header can add to what Weft sends and never
replace it.

Say how this weft is kept, how much is sent, and how much is held.

Setting ``history`` to ``memory`` does NOT reach out and delete anything. The stored
copy lives in a browser this service cannot see — the client erases its own copy
when it applies this.
Give this weft a voice, or clear it. All three fields or none.

get.description:
Always 200, always cheap, never authenticated.

Carries the degradation report so a misconfigured deploy is visible from a
curl instead of requiring a log dive. It deliberately exposes no counts,
versions, or paths — an unauthenticated caller learns only which subsystems
are up, which they would discover from a 503 anyway.
